name: Gabby Bernstein
currentValue: Named by Oprah as a 'next-generation thought leader.' The Universe Has Your Back sold 1M+ copies. Ten bestselling books. Co-hosted the Guinness World Records' largest guided meditation with Deepak Chopra. Named to Oprah's SuperSoul 100.
correction: Two factual issues: (1) 'Ten bestselling books' -- sources vary between 9 and 11 NYT bestsellers. Use '9+ NYT bestselling books' to be safe. (2) 'Co-hosted' the Guinness record meditation is exaggerated -- she was a 'special guest' alongside India Arie at Deepak Chopra's event (Aug 8, 2014, Toronto). Chopra led it. Correct to 'Featured as a special guest at Deepak Chopra's Guinness World Record largest guided meditation.' The 1M+ copies for Universe Has Your Back and Oprah SuperSoul 100 are confirmed.
source: GlobeNewsWire press releases (2014), Audible/Amazon author pages, Dopey Podcast ep 512.

name: Sam Harris
currentValue: Built the Waking Up app to $700K+ monthly revenue. Multiple New York Times bestselling books. His TED talks and podcast reach millions. Made rigorous, non-dual meditation practice accessible to a secular audience that would never set foot in an ashram or monastery.
correction: The $700K+ monthly revenue comes from Sensor Tower third-party estimates (March 2026), not official disclosure. Plausible but should be noted as an estimate, not confirmed revenue. All other claims are solid.
source: Sensor Tower data via networthspot.com, samharris.org.

name: Seane Corn
currentValue: Nightclub culture and addiction recovery meets yoga activism and social justice. She grew up borderline atheist in New Jersey, moved to New York at 17, worked in nightclubs (including Life Cafe with future Jivamukti co-founder David Life), struggled with addiction, then found yoga and turned it into a vehicle for frontline humanitarian work.
correction: Partially inaccurate: (1) 'Addiction recovery' overstates it -- sources describe casual/experimental substance use (marijuana, cocaine, drinking at age 19), not formal addiction and recovery in the clinical sense. (2) David Life was already the owner of Life Cafe when she worked there as a waitress -- calling him 'future Jivamukti co-founder' is technically correct but misleading in context. She worked alongside Sharon Gannon (fellow waitress) who co-founded Jivamukti with David Life. (3) She started yoga at 18 (1987) at Life Cafe. Born 1966 in Pompton Lakes, NJ -- these details are correct.
source: Everipedia, YogiTimes, Common Ground Magazine, Yogajala biography, Thrive Global.

name: Aubrey Marcus
currentValue: Built Onnit into a company that sold to Unilever for a reported $150 million+. Alpha Brain became one of the best-known nootropic supplements. His podcast reached millions. However, his personal brand became controversial -- his advocacy of open relationships, public separation from his wife after promoting their relationship as a model, and some of the wilder psychedelic content alienated parts of his audience. Post-Unilever acquisition, his cultural influence has diminished compared to his 2015-2019 peak.
correction: The '$150 million+' acquisition price is unverified. The Unilever-Onnit deal (April 26, 2021) was for an undisclosed amount. Third-party estimates range from $100M-$400M. The earlier claim in the bio section of '$100M+ revenue' is also unsupported -- documented revenue was ~$28M/year (Noah Kagan interview) and online revenue was ~$66M in 2024 (ECDB). Onnit was founded 2010, Alpha Brain launched July 2011. The editorial commentary about controversy is opinion, not fact-checkable. Recommend: 'Built Onnit into a company acquired by Unilever in 2021 for an undisclosed sum (estimated $100M-$400M).'
source: Crunchbase, Capitalism.com, Noah Kagan podcast ($28M revenue), Entrepreneur.com, ECDB ($66M online revenue 2024).

name: Ram Dass
currentValue: Rejected the Western academic framework for understanding consciousness. As Dr. Richard Alpert, he was a Harvard psychology professor running psilocybin experiments. When Harvard fired him, instead of defending his academic credentials, he abandoned his entire Western identity, went to India, and came back as Ram Dass -- a devotee, not a professor.
correction: Minor inaccuracies: (1) He was involved in both psilocybin AND LSD experiments (the Harvard Psilocybin Project), not just psilocybin. (2) Alpert was fired in 1963 specifically for giving drugs to an undergraduate student (procedural violation), not for the experiments themselves. Timothy Leary was not technically fired -- he resigned/was let go separately. The broad narrative is correct but the details should be tightened.
source: Wikipedia, Hudson Valley One, ScienceDirect, multiple biographical sources.

name: Marianne Williamson
currentValue: A Return to Love spent 39 weeks on the NYT bestseller list, hit #1 on Publishers Weekly for 11 weeks, sold over 1.5 million copies. Founded Project Angel Food, which has delivered over 14 million free meals to people with life-threatening illnesses. Named by Oprah as a defining spiritual voice of her generation.
correction: Two outdated figures: (1) '14 million meals' is outdated -- Project Angel Food now reports 18 million+ meals delivered. Update to '18 million+'. (2) '1.5 million copies' appears to be US-only; worldwide sales are reportedly 3 million+. The 39 weeks on NYT and #1 on Publishers Weekly for 11 weeks are confirmed by Wikipedia. The Oprah endorsement is confirmed.
source: Wikipedia (A Return to Love), Project Angel Food official site (angelfood.org), Oprah.com, marianne.com.

name: Yung Pueblo
currentValue: Grew from anonymous Instagram poetry account to 2.4 million followers. #1 New York Times bestselling author. Sold nearly 2 million books translated into 25+ languages. All built from free Instagram posts -- no paid ads, no publisher push, no traditional platform.
correction: Two issues: (1) Instagram followers are now 3 million+ (the 2.4M figure is outdated). (2) 'No paid ads, no publisher push, no traditional platform' is unverifiable and likely inaccurate -- his books are published by Harmony/Penguin Random House, a major publisher that does marketing. Remove 'no publisher push' claim. The 2M books sold and 25+ languages are confirmed by Penguin Random House.
source: Instagram @yung_pueblo (3M+), Penguin Random House author page, Audible bio.

name: Sri Sri Ravi Shankar
currentValue: Art of Living Foundation operates in 180 countries, with programs that have touched over 370 million people. Sudarshan Kriya, conceived during a 10-day silence in 1982, is now one of the most widely practiced breathing techniques on Earth. Multiple Nobel Peace Prize nominations.
correction: CRITICAL: 'Multiple Nobel Peace Prize nominations' is UNVERIFIED and likely false. Art of Living officially clarified that Sri Sri never claimed to have been offered/nominated for the Nobel Prize. Nobel nominations are secret for 50 years. There are advocacy campaigns (Change.org petitions, opinion articles) but no confirmed formal nominations. Remove this claim or change to 'Widely advocated for Nobel Peace Prize recognition.' Additionally, the '180 countries' figure is inconsistent -- Art of Living's own sources say 155 in some places, 182 in others. The '370 million people' comes from Art of Living marketing materials and is not independently verified.
source: Art of Living official clarification statement, Zee News, DailyO, Art of Living official site.

name: Sri Sri Ravi Shankar
currentValue: Ancient Vedic spiritual traditions meets modern mass-scale organizational management. He studied under Maharishi Mahesh Yogi (Transcendental Meditation), then built his own foundation with the operational scale and franchise-like consistency of a global corporation, standardizing sacred practices into repeatable, teachable weekend courses delivered identically across 180 countries.
correction: Minor: '180 countries' is inconsistent across Art of Living's own sources (155 vs 180 vs 182). Use 'over 150 countries' for safety. Core characterization is accurate.
source: Art of Living official site, Wikipedia.

name: Michael Singer
currentValue: The Untethered Soul became a multi-million copy NYT bestseller, translated into dozens of languages. Founded Medical Manager, acquired by WebMD for ~$5 billion. Founded Temple of the Universe, a yoga and meditation center that has operated continuously since 1975 -- over 50 years.
correction: Three issues: (1) Medical Manager acquisition was ~$4.8 billion in stock (per Computerworld), not '$5 billion' -- minor rounding but worth correcting. (2) He 'co-founded' Medical Manager (1981), not solely 'founded' it. (3) Singer was later prosecuted for securities fraud (2009 deferred prosecution agreement, $2.5M forfeiture) -- relevant omitted context. The Untethered Soul is confirmed as #1 NYT bestseller, translated into 45+ languages. Temple of the Universe (1975, Alachua FL) confirmed.
source: Computerworld ($4.8B deal), Wikipedia (Michael Alan Singer), DOJ press release, Temple of the Universe official site.

name: Michael Beckwith
currentValue: New Thought Christianity meets Eastern meditation and visionary practice. He was raised without a strong religious background, had a spontaneous spiritual awakening in his twenties, then built a spiritual community that blends affirmative prayer from New Thought with meditation, chanting, and practices drawn from Buddhism, Hinduism, and mystical Christianity.
correction: 'Raised without a strong religious background' is inaccurate. He grew up a Methodist but left at age 16. More critically, the twoWorlds field omits his most remarkable 'two worlds' element: before his spiritual awakening, he was a marijuana dealer at USC with distribution spanning DC, Atlanta, Nashville, NY, and LA. He was arrested for drug possession, and his incarceration prompted his spiritual transformation. The bio field correctly says 'former drug dealer' but this twoWorlds field misses the most dramatic collision of worlds. Suggest: 'Drug dealing and USC campus culture meets New Thought mysticism and Eastern meditation.'
source: BlackPast.org biography, Beyond Words blog, Wikipedia.

name: Michael Beckwith
currentValue: Grew Agape from a living room prayer group in 1986 to over 10,000 local members and 1 million+ online followers across 212 countries. Featured in The Secret. Spoke at the UN General Assembly. Co-founded Association for Global New Thought, hosting conferences with the Dalai Lama.
correction: '1 million+ online followers' is misleading. Agape's official site says '1 million unique hits annually' (website visits), which is very different from '1 million followers.' Correct to '1 million unique online visitors annually.' The 10,000 local members, 212 countries, The Secret feature, UN General Assembly appearance (World Interfaith Harmony Week), and Dalai Lama conferences are all confirmed.
source: Agape official site (agapelive.com), Wikipedia, Howard University chapel bio, The Secret IMDb.

name: Meghan Pappenheim
currentValue: Grew The Yoga Barn from two studios in 2007 to eight studios offering 20+ classes daily, making it the largest yoga studio complex in Indonesia. Co-created the BaliSpirit Festival (2008), now drawing 10,000+ visitors from 60+ countries annually. Spawned sister festivals in Hawaii, New Zealand, Ibiza, Mexico, Byron Bay, and Portugal.
correction: '10,000+ visitors' is inflated. Multiple sources (Windonesia 2016, 2025 travel review) report 7,000-8,000 attendees from 50-60 countries. Correct to '7,000-8,000 visitors from 50-60 countries.' Also '20+ classes daily' is understated -- recent sources say 25+ classes daily. The Yoga Barn growth from 2 to 8 studios is confirmed. Sister festivals list (Hawaii, New Zealand, Ibiza, Mexico, Byron Bay, Portugal) is confirmed.
source: Windonesia, ThisIsLuxuryTravel (2025 review), BaliSpirit Festival official site, APACentrepreneur profile.

name: Jeff Krasno
currentValue: Grew Wanderlust from 3,000 attendees at the first festival in 2009 to 130,000+ annual guests across 70+ events in 16 countries. Tripled attendance in year two (to 13,000), then scaled to 28 international markets by 2016. Later founded Commune, extending the model into digital community and education.
correction: Multiple number errors: (1) Year two attendance 'tripled to 13,000' is wrong -- SierraSun reports year two had 15,000 cumulative attendees (tripled from ~5,000 in year one, not 3,000). (2) '130,000+ annual guests' is inflated -- Fast Company/Eventbrite report ~120,000 tickets across ~70 events in 16 countries. (3) '28 international markets by 2016' is unverified and likely inflated -- documented figure is 16 countries. Suggest: 'Grew Wanderlust from ~5,000 attendees in 2009 to 120,000+ annual guests across 70+ events in 16 countries. Tripled to 15,000 in year two.'
source: SierraSun, Fast Company, Eventbrite case study, Wikipedia.

name: Larry Harvey
currentValue: Countercultural bohemian artist meets urban planner and philosophical architect. He grew up on a farm outside Portland, moved to San Francisco, and burned a wooden effigy on Baker Beach in 1986 after a painful breakup. Then spent the next 30 years turning that cathartic act into a philosophical framework for participatory culture, designing a 70,000-person temporary city in the desert governed by 10 self-organizing principles.
correction: Several factual issues: (1) 'Grew up on a farm outside Portland' is wrong -- he grew up in the Parkrose neighborhood of Portland (suburban, not a farm). Born in San Francisco, raised in Portland. (2) 'After a painful breakup' is contested. Jerry James attributed it to erasing a woman (Paula Peretti), but Harvey gave varying accounts. Mary Grauberger had been holding solstice bonfires on Baker Beach before 1986 and Harvey 'picked up the torch' when she stopped. The breakup-as-sole-origin is disputed. (3) 10 Principles were articulated in 2004, not at founding. (4) Peak attendance was 78,850 (2019), not '70,000'. Suggest: 'He grew up in suburban Portland, moved to San Francisco, worked as a landscaper and carpenter, and burned a wooden effigy on Baker Beach in 1986.'
source: Wikipedia, NPR obituary, Burning Man Journal, Washington Post obituary, Trippingly blog.

name: Larry Harvey
currentValue: Grew Burning Man from a bonfire on Baker Beach with a handful of friends (1986) to a 73,000-person temporary city in the Black Rock Desert. Spawned 100+ regional events in 20+ countries. Created a cultural movement that influenced Silicon Valley, the art world, and festival culture worldwide. The 10 Principles became a governance model studied by organizational theorists.
correction: '73,000-person' is understated -- peak attendance was 78,850 (2019) with an 80,000 cap. Use 'nearly 80,000' or '70,000+'. '100+ regional events in 20+ countries' dramatically understates the regional network -- Burning Man's own site says events in 'over 100 countries,' not '20+ countries.' Correct to '100+ regional events across 100+ countries.' Cultural influence claims are well-documented.
source: Burning Man Project official site, Wikipedia, YourEDM, Expanded Ramblings.
